questions.q: What are the four steps of the WRAP process?
a: Widen options, reality-test, attain distance, prepare to be wrong
Write it down, review it, act on it, praise the outcome
Weigh options, research facts, ask others, proceed quickly
Wonder, reflect, accept, persist through setbacks
questions.why: The overview lists the four WRAP elements used for important decisions.

questions.q: Why is a simple yes-or-no decision usually a mistake?
a: It ignores the other options and their opportunity costs
It takes far longer than comparing many choices
It relies too heavily on advice from friends
It always leads to the most expensive outcome
questions.why: Lesson 1 says binary thinking hides the many possible alternatives and what they cost.

questions.q: What happened when the option to decline a $14.99 video was labeled "keep the money"?
a: The share of people declining rose from 25 to 45 percent
The share of people declining fell from 45 to 25 percent
Nearly everyone bought the video anyway
The price of the video was immediately lowered
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the study to show that naming opportunity costs changes choices.

questions.q: What does the Heath brothers' term "ooching" mean?
a: Testing a decision on a small scale before committing
Delaying a decision until all uncertainty disappears
Copying what a successful friend decided to do
Making a choice quickly to avoid overthinking
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends small trials, like starting a blog before quitting your job.

questions.q: What question does the 10/10/10 perspective ask?
a: How will you feel about this in 10 minutes, 10 months and 10 years?
How much will this cost in 10 minutes, 10 months and 10 years?
How many people will be affected after 10 days, 10 weeks and 10 years?
What would 10 friends, 10 experts and 10 strangers advise?
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the 10/10/10 trick as a way to gain emotional distance.
